data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 asserts that independent failures follow a Poisson distribution and shared-cause failures exhibit temporal synchronicity, but this mechanism confuses the symptom (temporal clustering) with the cause. The problem demands a causal mechanism that distinguishes truly independent failures from merely-appearing-uncorrelated ones. Poisson-distributed arrival times can still produce coincidental bursts that mimic synchronicity, and, conversely, a shared latent cause (e.g., a slow-propagating misconfiguration) can produce staggered, non-synchronous failures that look independent. The countercondition about cascade propagation partially concedes this, but the core mechanism still fails to provide the causal evidence the problem requires because it relies on statistical pattern-matching rather than establishing an actual causal link to a shared root cause.
